final_answer: When the mRNA vaccine is injected into the body, the mRNA enters the cells and is not incorporated into the cell's DNA, remaining safe. The mRNA contains instructions for the cells to produce a protein found on the surface of the virus, which is harmless and safe. Once the protein is produced, it is displayed on the surface of the cells, signaling to the immune system that a foreign invader is present, which is safe. The immune system then responds by producing antibodies and memory cells to fight the virus, which is safe.
